notes.title: Knowing the Basics!
notes.notes:
[u][b]Basic Movement[/b][/u]
Movement in Eagle Island Twist follows a simple left and right horizontal scheme. When you run either way and suddenly change direction, your character will do a brief slide, then start running in that new direction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/d46498cb7b22bd24aa93770833ba5c1d83dca615.gif[/img]
[u][b]Jumping & Grabbing[/b][/u]
Jumping allows Quill and Fia to reach higher areas normally out of reach, which could allow them to grab onto a ledge and further access what was once inaccessible at lower heights. Certain runestones can further increase their jump height, along with being able to evade incoming projectiles and special enemy types.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/e9ee339755131220d370bc1e8f956a0e2e23e807.gif[/img]
[u][b]Aiming[/b][/u]
Quill and Fia utilize a multi-directional aim. However, their range to throw Koji/Kusako respectively is limited without the proper runestone! Players can take advantage of this directional aim to hit enemies beyond narrow pathways, traveling midair by hitting enemy to enemy, or to get a good angle to eliminate multiple enemies at once.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/f038f03122efc385370cd3a2dc60bde895d493dd.gif[/img]
[u][b]Attacking with different Elements and Maintaining Manaroc[/b][/u]
Quill and Fia can attack by launching their flying companions at targets. Each owl can imbue itself with elemental powers to increase their potency and utility across different levels.
Below are just some of the many elemental forms you can have Koji or Kusako change into!
[olist]
[*][b]Magira Form[/b]: The fire form. Excellent damage output and great for attacking multiple enemies at once.
[*][b]Icora Form[/b]: The ice form. Can slow down enemies hit by Koji or Kusako, or freeze them for a brief amount of time, leaving them open to attack!
[*][b]Zephara Form[/b]: The lightning form. Covers Koji or Kusako in an electrified aura, allowing them to travel in a straight line aimed at any direction. This form allows Koji and Kusako to travel through and damage multiple enemies in a line.
[/olist]In addition, each use of any elemental form depletes a set amount of Manarocs in the player’s bar. In order to use certain elemental forms, players must have the necessary Manaroc amounts to use. In the examples below, each time Fia throws Kusako, while imbued with an element, she will lose one Manaroc–as indicated by the disappearing blue icon in the top left.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/77b93f6de67b5b8089608a882b0d9945b7566cb1.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/52cc12917a0d41e0b261407a955d33403a10eccb.gif[/img]
[u][b]Switching between Elements[/b][/u]
Koji and Kusako are able to switch between multiple element types, increasing their potency and utility across different levels. Knowing when to use the Magira type over the Icora type could prove essential to defeating certain enemies, as well as maintaining your manarocs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/8cb1bb718af82e9c202173741a2ad90fb32e861f.gif[/img]
Time to explore all of Yulu with Quill and Fia! [i]Eagle Island Twist[/i] is available NOW!

notes.title: Patch 2.0.3.4
notes.notes:
A very minor patch in preparation for this weekend's speedrun tournament.

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Workaround: In rare circumstances the urchin at the end of Prickletack Pond could despawn itself. As a workaround for the tournament, if this happens the Manaroc Shard will now spawn in automatically at 13 seconds in the boss room or later. This will be fixed properly in the next major patch.
[*] Fixed: The secret code was not displayed when playing the game in German language.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 2.0.3.3
notes.notes:
Thanks to all the players who provided early feedback on Discord. A quick patch with a few QoL features and some fixes :)

[h3]Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] Speedrun timer now continues to run on the menu and map
[*] Speedrun timer now shows an individual level timer
[/list]

[h3]Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] The combo-crystal puzzle in Ice Slide Glide has been redesigned to stop players misinterpreting the solution.
[*] A manaroc block has been added to the challenge at the end of Thrust Jump Jeopardy to help players find the solution.
[*] In Hardcore difficulty, blocks which contained hearts on easier difficulties now appears as solid empty blocks instead of breakable blocks. This was misleading players into thinking secrets were nearby.
[*] Off-screen seeds in Sploding Seeds now have an arrow indicator
[*] Minor tweaks to a few levels
[*] Ice Shard Missiles on Ancient Armaments now despawn if you enter a room and one is near Fia.
[*] Sound effects no longer play on repeat when stationary on the Twist map screen.
[*] The clinking cog sound effect of falling platforms is no long audible when in other rooms.
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed: It was not possible to gain a gold medal on Ribbilick Ruins. The coin requirement has been lowered.
[*] Fixed: The game soft-locks when health reaches zero in lava, when trapped beneath a platform.
[*] Fixed: The game could occaisional crash on first load due to an issue creating the config.ini file.
[*] Fixed: Spamming different feather selection when flying through a room exit could cause Kusako to teleport backwards in Flying Solo.
[*] Fixed: Kusako could clip inside the terrain when taking damage in Flying Solo.
[*] Fixed: Manaroc Twist Shards could be bounced around by explosions, causing them to land in inaccessible areas.
[*] Fixed: Sometimes new paths appeared offset after beating a level and returning to the map screen.
[/list]

It’s been a long flight, but after a lot of hard work and lost feathers, Eagle Island Twist is out today!

[previewyoutube=oz1JTHVQBx4;full][/previewyoutube]

This massive update takes the awesome mechanics of the original Eagle Island, and builds on them in fresh and inventive ways across an expansion that is practically a new game!

About Twist: 
Eagle Island Twist is a free update that brings an all-new story to Eagle Island. As Fia, use your kookaburra Kusako to embark on an adventure that has you facing off against a dark doppelganger to restore a broken artifact - the Manaroc Twist! On your journey you’ll encounter extraordinary challenges, huge bosses, and awesome new powers, as you track down Dark Fia.

Jam packed with new content, Eagle Island Twist brings the high-flying action of the original game to new heights!

New Levels, New Challenges:
Explore over 45 handcrafted stages that mix up the gameplay and pay homage to classic retro titles. Choose between casual or more difficult routes via the branching world map, and replay levels to find hidden collectables and secret areas.

notes.title: Eagle Island Summer Solstice Update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, welcome to the Eagle Island Summer Solstice Update!

I've been paying close attention to reviews and feedback, and challenged myself to create this update fixing all of the key issues players had with the game! Here's a fun video showing the update's features. If you stick around for the end, you'll get a preview of what's coming next!

[previewyoutube=2Pg3S9wGO5Q;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Revamped player control[/h2]
You said Quill's movement was too slippery and unresponsive. I originally wanted Quill to feel like a retro game character, but this clashed with many players' expectation of an indie game. I've now increased Quill's acceleration (so he's not slippery) and added a skidding animation with dust clouds, making him feel more grounded. His air acceleration has also been increased to give greater control while jumping (a bit less Simon Belmont!)

You also said Koji took too long to recover after missing a shot - this recovery time has been significantly reduced.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/873f7a4116916264d4e5709ced650df47eb2c9fb.gif[/img]

[h2]Revamped aiming system[/h2]
You said aiming Koji was too difficult and the 8 direction aiming felt bad. I've reprogrammed the entire aiming system making it more responsive - for both keyboard and gamepad. I removed a feature which snaps the direction you aim back to horizontal - this was causing many players to inadvertently launch Koji horizontally when they didn't want to. The game now defaults to 360 aiming when using a gamepad, and has a new (optional) aiming guide to keep your aim true! If you want to use 360 aiming without a gamepad, you can either enable mouse control or use the auto aim accessibility feature.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/4e10cdfc4ba83278dae617ad193687fd0c1104a3.gif[/img]

[h2]New runestones[/h2]
You said some of the runestones are too boring. I've replaced those ones with 17 brand new ones! I've also buffed some of the remaining runestones to make them more exciting and practical. Runestones now display a life bar on the UI so you aren't surprised when they suddenly explode! As before, there's the option to make them permanent if you prefer that. Toucan Traders now carry an extra runestone in their stock so you get a greater choice at shops!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/ead5db58f1c5d3d0e7a250c54d9f93d61bfe4308.gif[/img]

[h2]Damage and checkpoints[/h2]
You said the game is too hard and should have checkpoints to respawn at. It's traditional in a roguelite to restart a run from the beginning if you fail, but I totally understand that many players don't like that. Now you can enable respawning and simply start from the last fast travel statue you activated! There's also the option to completely disable taking damage. These options are available on all difficulty settings and can be enabled/disabled on the fly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/8e96460b19267c3a057f7377b122cc042f68f844.gif[/img]

[h2]Effects and graphics[/h2]
Koji's had a bit of a graphical update with a smoother turning around animation and a much bouncier squishy impact animation! Fire, lightning and ice effects have all been greatly improved - the game is much flashier now.

Thanks to you all for playing, and stay tuned for more big news coming soon!

Adjustment: Achievements now allowed with Gameplay Tweaks turned on

notes.title: Eagle Island review
notes.notes:
Eagle Island is about exploring a mysterious shapeshifting island while pelting its exotic wildlife to death with a docile bird. Is this how falconry works? I don’t know. But you’re definitely using a lovely creature as live ammunition, which is a bit of a shock at first. And then, after the shock wears off, actually pretty funny.

Quill is the main character, a cherubic pixel boy with a penchant for avian-led assault. Having witnessed the abduction of his pet owl Ichiro, he’s forced to traverse a gorgeous island with his remaining pet, Koji, in order to save it. The island is a dreamlike blend of airy waterside exteriors and moody caves, and the game’s structure is a refreshing hybrid of Metroidvania and roguelike. The overworld is static, but each sidescrolling dungeon is randomised. 

Birds of Prey

It’s not a roguelike, though. Overworld progress, as well as certain major abilities and bird attack types, stay unlocked permanently. It’s inside dungeons where the roguelike aspect rears its head: Dungeons contain another tier of abilities that are lost upon death, alongside all progress made towards an inevitable boss. The dungeon abilities comprise various buffs and bonuses, and each takes up one of four available ability slots. Upon death, all slotted abilities are lost, as is any currency accrued in the dungeon. 

It actually works really well, to begin with: Those averse to the crushing loss of progress associated with roguelikes don’t have much to fear, because while the difficulty of the dungeons does ramp up significantly, there’s never the risk of losing a dungeon ability that strengthens the odds in your favour. Very few do. It's a bit of a relief, but also a problem for Eagle Island as it unfolds.

Combat is all about tossing Koji at all manner of native wildlife: Raging boars, angry fish, pleasant looking sentient flowers. Quill can only toss in one of eight directions, and at first this limitation feels stifling. Once adjusted to (with a controller—keyboard is not recommended for this game), the combat in Eagle Island can feel like a whimsically violent take on snooker. Each toss of Koji allows a short midair pause, and downing foes in rapid succession provides combo bonuses which can provide mana and, very rarely, replenish health.  

Chirp off the old block

As a bird-loving shoot-em-up, Eagle Island works, and there’s no doubting how beautiful it is: both overworld and dungeon are brimming with lively animation and detail. But it’s ultimately shallower than it first appears. The first hour or so is spent unlocking an additional three attack types for Koji, which add fire, ice and electricity effects. Apart from situations where they’re required to solve breezy puzzles, I rarely used these more powerful attacks during moment-to-moment combat.

The scarcity of the mana required to use them, combined with the awkwardness of switching between attacks mid-combat, makes them feel useless most of the time. 

That applies to the looted dungeon abilities too, which range from the ability to pirouette higher into the air, more rapid recovery for Koji, and various buffs to drop rates, among many others. Aside from a small handful of abilities—in particular, one that turns Koji into a homing missile—these tend to feel insignificant. None will flip the fate of your run. It’s possible to expand your maximum HP, and I invariably spent my cash on that, rather than abilities. 

The dullness of the abilities undermines the light roguelike approach Eagle Island’s dungeons take, and while the level randomisation is a neat way to keep things fresh, it can’t hide the fact that, 90 percent of the time, you’re basically playing an 8-directional shooter (with a bird!). 

The completion of dungeons unlocks permanent abilities that allow Quill to explore the overworld, and this is where the Metroidvania elements creep in. I loved this (very light) exploration in the overworld. On the other hand, the compulsion to explore the meandering dungeons is virtually non-existent because, basically, none of the in-dungeon abilities are worth straying off the beaten path for. 

So Eagle Island is a slightly confused hybrid of a game: The movement, combat, mood and setting I loved, but it’s all hampered by dull abilities and a roguelike touch that doesn’t feel necessary. I reckon I’ll still boot Eagle Island up occasionally to feel the gracefulness of its movement and combat, but it’s hard to recommend to anyone but platformer diehards.

notes.title: Lite Mode Update beta
notes.notes:
Hey, I've been listening to your feedback and I've just finished developing a big patch, and it's available now in a public beta. Just choose the public_beta branch for Eagle Island (there's a how-to GIF at the bottom).

It includes a new difficulty mode, Lite, which only requires a 3x combo to earn health. Additionally, you'll be able to keep unused runestones and apply them as a loadout in future runs! You'll also get the chance to win extra runestones on the game over screen depending on how many monster's you've defeated.

I've also added a 360 degree aiming mode for Koji. This is a departure from Eagle Island's core design and may unbalance the game for you, but it's here for you to try!

Why not jump into the [url=https://discord.gg/EagleIsland]official Eagle Island Discord server[/url] and tell me what you think?

All this comes with a whole bunch of other fixes and tweaks, check out the changelog:
[list]
[*]Add: New Lite difficulty setting
[*]Add: Store unwanted perks in the backpack
[*]Add: Lucky Chance on game over
[*]Add: Select loadout from backpack on new run
[*]Add: 360 degree aiming Gameplay Tweak
[*]Add: Permanent runestones Gameplay Tweak
[*]Fix: Spamming change feather while performing double jumps could soft lock Quill
[*]Fix: Urchidna could hide behind large coral
[*]Fix: Keys could sink to the bottom of water before Quill can swim
[*]Fix: Toucan Trader shop items weren’t consistent on seeded levels
[*]Fix: Venom and Potam projectiles sometimes stop bouncing
[*]Fix: Lantern chains could break apart and shake
[*]Fix: Icora’s Wrath could last forever when using Icora Lock
[*]Fix: Soft lock in Armaura battles when attacking from below the camera’s bottom edge
[*]Fix: Graphical error in gold Rattit’s tail
[*]Fix: Oliver’s hit sprite was facing the wrong way when facing right
[*]Fix: The shop button hint text did not update after buying an item
[*]Fix: Mushroom monsters’ gas cloud hitboxes did not match their animation
[*]Fix: Ancient Coin slot was shown, but empty, after completing The Lair
[*]Fix Linux/Mac: GIF and screenshot features would crash the game
[*]Fix Switch: Could not scroll down text boxes
[*]Fix GOG: Achievements didn’t work when offline
[*]Adjustment: Enhanced throw angles when using the thumbstick
[*]Adjustment: Revamped difficulty screen
[*]Adjustment: Option to change difficulty on Game Over (story mode)
[*]Adjustment: Option to change difficult on Win (story mode)
[*]Adjustment: Quill can now run while up or down is being held
[*]Adjustment: Fire Trail runestone replaced with Ember runestone
[*]Adjustment: Volcanic Bomb runestone no longer sets the ground alight
[*]Adjustment: Mushboom runestone explosions no longer hurt Quill
[*]Adjustment: Can now launch Koji while in a ledge grab
[*]Adjustment: Can now hit Burroph’s tail while it is retreating
[*]Adjustment: New Game Plus button now has a description
[*]Adjustment: Time locked doors in Fireside Forest and High Tide Trouble are more forgiving
[*]Adjustment: Overworld map now shows secret levels and ancient coins
[*]Adjustment: Increase amount of items given for Offering runestone
[*]Adjustment: Iframes added after Blast Off and Stratosphere

[/list]

notes.title: The first updates
notes.notes:
Thanks to everyone who's been supportive and provided feedback so far! There have been a few patches already - you can check the changelog [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/681110/discussions/0/1639790664931161137/]here[/url]. Most fixes involve making the minecarts easier.

[b]What's coming soon in v1.0.8.0?[/b]
I've received a LOT of feedback over the last few days, and one thing is very clear. Players are divided into two main categories: those who want to challenge themselves to learn the game/mechanics, and those who would rather go through the game with less challenge (presumably with a more Mario-like difficulty).

For those in the first category (want a challenge and learn the game/mechanics), not too much is changing. I'm patching and fixing any unfair parts so you won't be cheated.

For the latter category, I'm introducing a new difficulty mode - Lite. In this mode you'll be able to gain health by attaining a 3x combo (instead of 4x). You'll be offered the option (but not necessarily encouraged) to change the difficulty after having a few game-overs on a level. You'll have some bonus HP while fighting overworld bosses.

A question to prospective Lite difficulty players - would you like blue chests to contain 1 heart as well as gaining hearts from 3x combos? I need to make sure this mode has the correct settings and your feedback is required!

It'll go live on a beta branch - more info coming soon.

notes.title: Wot I Think: Eagle Island
notes.notes:
Developer: Pixelnicks
Publisher: Screenwave Media
Release: Out now
On: Windows, Mac
From: Steam
Price: 15.49, $20, 16.79

I’m a bit torn, readers. Eagle Island has a lot going for it. It looks lovely, for one, with a rich palette fully enlivening some classic game environments. Everything sounds great, and on paper its design is timeless, as you explore an island level by level, unlocking more powers with each defeated boss. And its novel weapon should be a huge draw – instead of jumping on heads or hacking or bashing monsters, you throw an owl at them, either as is or after upgrading it with magical feathers.

But I don’t like it. I’m still playing it after two days, but not because I’m hooked. It’s because it never quite stops annoying me.

(more…)

notes.title: Eagle Island, a platformer about owl-hurling, is out now
notes.notes:
Back in 2017 a falconry-themed platformer called Eagle Island caught our eye on Kickstarter, thanks to its central mechanic which has you throwing an owl at your enemies. Eagle Island went on to make its goal, spent the last couple of years in development, and is out now.

The setup has it that one of your owl friends named Koji has been abducted by a giant eagle, and so you take your remaining owl and your magical gauntlet, then head to Eagle Island to perform a daring rescue. The owl can be powered up with elemental totem feathers and there are power-up runes to collect as well. If you've ever wanted to bust a hole in a wall by throwing an owl at it this is the game for you.

Eagle Island has procedurally generated levels, 12 bosses, and three modes—story, roguelite, and speedrun. You can get it on Steam.

notes.title: Eagle Island is out!
notes.notes:
Eagle Island is LIVE! YES - it’s true! Thank you so much for your patience in this journey. My first video game is now available for you to play!

I’ve dreamed of being able to complete and launch a game for most of my life. With your excitement fueling my programming, it’s finally a reality. Not only did Eagle Island successfully fund on Kickstarter way back in 2017 the release on Steam, but it’s available on Nintendo Switch (NA) eShop right now, too! It’s been an amazing learning experience, of course. For example, Nintendo Switch (EU) eShop isn’t live yet (but it will be on July 16) - turns out the certification can be a real pain in the feathers.

Regardless - Thank you for playing and supporting Eagle Island. 

Keep an eye out for merch soon!

notes.title: Umm.. Welcome to “Award-Winning” Eagle Island?!?
notes.notes:
We’ve received some great news ahead of announcing our launch date! 

Eagle Island was on display for a record-breaking attendance at MomoCon 2019. Over 39,000 gaming and animation fans made their way through the convention centre to play titles including a brilliant lineup of indie developed projects.

YouTuber Jesse Cox hosted the 5th Annual Indie Games Showcase recognising 20 indie titles on the showroom floor. The judges, Rami Ismail (Vlambeer), Mike Fahey (Kotaku), Chris Carter (Destructoid), Austin Wood (PC Gamer), and Janet Garcia (IGN), gather to select the top 5 games at MomoCon 2019! Amongst the standouts, Eagle Island was named an “Indie Winner!” 

It’s an honour to be awarded and include with other great titles. 

We’re really, really excited to get the launch Eagle Island. Stay tuned - launch date will be announced [i]very soon[/i]. 😁

[img]https://i.imgur.com/p1eE4Ur.png[/img]

notes.title: The Owl Has Landed - Demo now available!
notes.notes:
Eagle Island is on the way - it’s HAPPENING! 

It’s safe to say we underestimated the amount of time behind proper QA and testing, but the support we’ve had in the past year has been.. owl-mazing - thank you to those in the [url=https://discord.gg/EagleIsland]Discord[/url] and on [url=https://twitter.com/pixelnicks]Twitter[/url] for joining our high-spirited community.

With an [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/681110/Eagle_Island/]official demo[/url] now available on Steam, we’re on track to speaking publicly to a very exciting launch date announcement in the coming weeks! After taking Eagle Island to conventions and putting it in the hands of reviewers, soon Koji and Quill will be available for everyone to play at home.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Ffv3auz.gif[/img]

If you haven’t yet - get your hands on the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/681110/Eagle_Island/]demo[/url]! Every run generates a new map - who knows what you’ll come across on your next crawl.

Keep an eye out for the Eagle Island launch trailer and date in the coming weeks! Thanks for sharing the experience with me.

notes.title: Eagle Island is feature complete and approaching launch!
notes.notes:
Hey there, prospective falconers!

Eagle Island is finally feature complete! I just need to get through the testing phase to ensure the product you receive is bug-free and super smooth!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/YIVyM9Q.gif[/img]

If you want to join the community, chat with other fans or testers, or even myself (I'm Nick), hop into the [url=https://discord.gg/ddk2kPT ]Eagle Island Discord server[/url].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/BzJAh4v.gif[/img]

Here's a recap of what you'll find in the game:

[list]
[*] 9 biomes, with a total of 16 visually different environments
[*] An impressive and unique level generation system
[*] Story mode with 19 procedurally generated levels
[*] Rogue mode with 16 configured run styles
[*] 85 runestone perks to randomize your character build
[*] 10 main bosses, and 3 special story mode boss battles
[*] Each main boss has 4 difficulty settings, making future encounters more intense
[*] Boss Rush mode, which is crazy fun
[*] Weekly Speedrun mode, where you can challenge other players to the fastest completion time on a short run
[/list]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/JFJaMx3.gif[/img]

I tried so hard, but we have [i]just missed[/i] the window for releasing in 2018. This is disappointing for all of us, but it does mean I can spend a little time giving the game that extra layer of polish before a launch in the new year!
